$comment: A PROPOSAL, NOT A WRITE. Nothing here has been applied to any item; misconception-taxonomy still FAILS on all 66, which is the honest state. What CHANGED on 2026-10-04 is that the taxonomy it proposes against is no longer DRAFT: Sean read the v1 version of this file, and directed the two additions that v1's own measurements argued for. This is the re-measurement against v2.
status: PARTLY APPLIED 2026-10-04 on Sean's authorisation — the 48 clean fits are in the bank (authoring/misconception-tags-batch-1.json). 14 are HELD because the fit is approximate or needs two families; writing a family on a near-fit records a guess in the one field the analytics layer trusts. 4 are for REWRITE, not tagging.
drafted: 2026-10-04 (v1), re-measured against taxonomyVersion 2 the same day
draftedBy: Claude. An authoring agent may not approve its own work.
whatSeansDecisionBought: v1 measured 33 of 66 clean, 13 approximate, 13 UNRESOLVED and 6 NOT CLASSIFIABLE AT ALL. v2 measures 52 of 66 clean, 13 approximate, 1 needing two families, and ZERO of either failing category. The polarity-reversal family (MC-F-15) absorbed 12 of the 13 unresolved and is now the second-most-cited family in the bank; the distractorFunction axis absorbed all 6 that were not families, plus the 13th unresolved case (PS-0090/B, which turned out to be a partial-truth). Nothing was forced: the 13 approximate fits are unchanged and still say so.

whatIsStillOpen.finding: MEANS TAKEN FOR ENDS — three cases, still no family that fits. US.05-GEN-02/C ('mistakes a method of assimilation for its purpose') and q-us45-dok1-1/D ('mistakes an instrument of the New Deal for one of its three aims') are the SAME error and are filed to MC-F-04 and MC-F-13 respectively, which is the aggregation failure in miniature. Three occurrences is thin evidence for a 16th family; recorded so the next round counts rather than re-derives. Unchanged from v1.

MC-F-07 (Presentism) IS WRITTEN IN ONE DIRECTION ONLY — 'applies present-day values to historical actors'. PS-0067/C is the reverse: the student assumes the past was LESS capable than it was (the Culebra Cut was dug with steam shovels). Widening that statement to cover both directions costs nothing and makes one assignment clean.

ONE DISTRACTOR NEEDS TWO FAMILIES. PSTIM-0124/C is a wrong ACTOR (MC-F-02) caused by wrong TIMING (MC-F-01). The schema takes one; either is defensible and the choice changes what a report says the student needs. Flagged rather than decided.

RESOLVED 2026-10-04: Sean applied the CCR rule to this bank. `plausible-fabrication` is now `itemFlaw: true`, so the 4 distractors using it are REWRITTEN rather than tagged — anchored in something that really happened and is wrong for THIS stem, never a different invented claim. ⚠ One of the four exposes bad history in its OWN misconception label: PSTIM-0041/B is recorded as 'invents a negotiated settlement for the blockade', but the Berlin Blockade WAS ended by negotiation — the Jessup-Malik talks at the UN and the New York Agreement of May 1949. The false parts of that option are 'peace treaty' and 'permanent zones', not the existence of a settlement. The label is corrected with the rewrite.

whatIsNotProposedHere: No item is modified. The 66 findings stand until the write is authorised.
No further family or function is added. F4 and F5 are proposals for a later read; a model adding to a taxonomy it was asked to apply would be approving its own work.
No IRT or calibration claim. A family says nothing about item difficulty.
